name: English

scheme.name: Penn Treebank (revised; NML nodes, split hyphens)

samples.text: I saw the man with a telescope.
samples.note: Ambiguous: the telescope can be the instrument of seeing or belong to the man. The parser returns one reading; the Algorithm Lab can show both.

samples.text: Did the students not read the book that the professor recommended?
samples.note: Yes/no question with negation and a relative clause.

samples.text: She arrived late because the train was delayed, but the meeting had not started.
samples.note: Coordination, a subordinate clause, and a passive.

notes: Dependency analyses follow Universal Dependencies v2 (Stanza model trained on UD English corpora). Measured on UD English-EWT test: LAS 89.7 (in-domain).
Constituency trees follow Penn Treebank conventions (e.g. NN, VBD, SBAR), which differ from many introductory textbook trees (e.g. N, V, X-bar levels). Labels are shown as the parser produced them.
The parser returns a single analysis even for ambiguous sentences.

The dependency and constituency analyses come from two independent models. On ambiguous sentences they can choose different readings (e.g. in "I don't like the man with a telescope" the dependency model attaches "telescope" to the verb, while the constituency model attaches the PP to "the man"). Neither view is derived from the other.
